slides.title: A sender in a costume
slides.text: Pim sorts a message that claims to be from the school office. The name on it looks right, but a claimed sender is a costume. That faking is called spoofing, and the real address tells the truth.
slides.alt: A Pro trick card: the sender name looks friendly, but a faked name is exactly what spoofing means.

focus.cue: The name says Your bank; the badge says unknown sender
A claimed sender is a costume: read the whole card

slides.title: Where does the link go?
slides.text: The words on a link can say one name while the address behind them goes somewhere else. Check the address, not the words.
steps: Address behind them: a stranger's place
Do not tap; verify another way
slides.alt: A trick wearing a bank's name: for your safety, it says, confirm your mailbox key and your birthday.

focus.cue: A sender can write any name on an envelope
Says the bank, but the badge says unknown sender

slides.title: Aimed at one person
slides.text: Spear phishing uses the same trick recipe, but built for one person. It may use your name, your club or a recent post, then add a rush and a request.
slides.alt: A fan club card that knows too much: your dog's name and your birthday, learned from your public profile.

focus.cue: Built for one person: it knows your dog's name
Knows things from your public profile

slides.title: The attachment rule
slides.text: An unexpected file is not opened, even if the message begs you to hurry. Verify first through a different door: ask the real sender in person, or tell a trusted adult.
slides.alt: A parcel trick: a delivery you never ordered is waiting, and a small fee must be paid within two hours.

focus.cue: An unexpected parcel, with a pay-now button
Asks for money, two hours to act

slides.title: Reporting protects everyone
slides.text: Reporting a phishing message is a Defender act. One report can warn the whole school and stop the same costume reaching your friends.
slides.alt: A trick wearing a bank's name: for your safety, it says, confirm your mailbox key and your birthday.

focus.cue: The badge shows whether the post office really knows them
Safe, trick, or ask a trusted adult: report it

words.means: pretending to be a sender you trust
fake messages that fish for taps, replies or secrets
a fake message built for one person, using details about them
a file sent along with a message

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Packet Post at Spot the Trick: the same Pro cards you checked in step 3.3, so this step is already earned when the game opens. For every message, check the real sender before you judge it.
slides.alt: A Pro trick card: the sender name looks friendly, but a faked name is exactly what spoofing means.

focus.cue: Check the real sender before you judge each card
